text:
elaine: Heads-up — planning a coordinated base-image rebuild next Wed 09:00 PST to address CVE-2026-1423 and to tighten runtime permissions. Need quick checks: RBAC changes, KMS signing flow, and audit-log retention.

sam: +1. Do we have a KMS key ready for cosign signing or do we rotate? Also need to confirm prow/buildkite workers can access signing role.

arun: We should avoid creating a new long-lived key. Recommend an ephemeral signing key for the rebuild tasks bound to a short-lived role token. Rotation window = 30d.

jess: Vulnerability triage status: CVE-2026-1423 is in libc layer. Patch available in upstream alpine 3.18.2. Impact: privileged runtime processes can escalate. I want to add a runtime denial policy for CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the pod profiles.

elaine: ok noted. RBAC question: we want to remove broad pull/push on gcr://redwood-images for the devs group. Instead create a deployer role and a separate signing role for CI. Thoughts?

sam: +thumbsup: split is good. Also add an audit binding so every push is logged to the centralized audit project with the image digest.

oliver: For incident response — let's add a new runbook section for rollout rollback based on image signature validation failing in staging. Link to draft runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/rebuild-runtime-guardrails (please don't share externally).

jess: From vuln side, we want an automated canary: build+scan -> canary deploy -> runtime exploit smoke-tests (privilege escalation checks) -> prod promotion. If scan fails, block signing.

image-scan-bot: scan report for branch/rebuild-2026-03: base-image:alpine-3.18.2: HIGH: CVE-2026-1423 fixed, MEDIUM: openssl outdated -> upgrade to 3.0.8. Full report: https://scans.internal/scan/2521239876

sam: Example cosign with KMS (for ops CI):
```
cosign sign --kms gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/signing/cryptoKeys/rebuild-ephemeral \
  --annotations "build=base-rebuild-2026-03" gcr.io/redwood-images/base:2026-03-10
```

arun: Add IAM condition: allow cosign signer role only from the CI service account and only for the specific keyRing resource. Also enforce least-privilege for token exchange.

elaine: Audit logging: retention proposal = 180 days for image-push/pull events, 365 days for signing events. We also need immutable logs for 90 days per compliance. Any objections?

jess: 180/365 sounds fine. We should add an automatic alert if a non-whitelisted key signs an image.

oliver: Ops note: during rollout please keep a 2-hour canary window, we will monitor pod-level seccomp/ebpf denies. If see a pattern of denies that map to legitimate app behavior, escalate to app-owner and create an allowlist CR.

sam: Who will make the RBAC IAM changes? I can open the CR for IAM changes, but need the exact binding names.

elaine: @sam please create the PR with bindings: roles/redwood.imageDeployer -> serviceAccount:deploy@redwood, roles/redwood.imageSigner -> serviceAccount:ci-sign@redwood, and audit sink -> projects/redwood-audit. Tag me and @arun.

jess: I'll pin the vulnerability tests and add them to the canary pipeline (smoke: privilege-escalation, suid-check, network egress test).

image-scan-bot: queued full rebuild scan: https://scans.internal/scan/2521239876/queue-id-9987

arun: Also: add KMS key metadata to signing annotations (key-id + key-hash) so we can detect unexpected keys in provenance.

elaine: Great. Next steps: sam opens IAM PR by EOD Friday, jess wires canary tests, arun drafts the KMS ephemeral key policy, oliver updates runbook. We'll sync Tue 10:30 for final go/no-go.

sam: Will do. 

jess: Thanks, all.

oliver: :white_check_mark:

image-scan-bot: result: initial scan queued, will post results here.
